brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 holds the base cells (full at 0,0; 1,0 half-e; -1,0; 0,1; 1,-1 half-n, plus drawer frame notches at -1,1 and 0,-1). Level 1 holds full pieces at 0,0,1; -1,0,1; 0,1,1, stacked on the ground storey. check_build reports ok with meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: For a workbench, at least two drawers
requirements.evidence: Two slide drawers: drawer:0#1,0#cut on the cut face of the half-e base at 1,0,0 and drawer:0#1,-1#cut on the cut face of the half-n base at 1,-1,0. Both are seated on half-base cut faces as the configurator requires.

finish.summary: The build is a two-storey hex tower: a ground storey with two slide drawers (on half bases at 1,0 and 1,-1) plus drawer-frame notches, and an upper storey of three full bases. check_build returns ok with meshClash clear and no rule errors. Remaining items are info-only open cap faces; I did not add covers or caps, and no load claims are made.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
